post.summary: Move a project to another server
post.description: With dryRun, only the checks run. Otherwise the live commit is deployed on the target server through the deploy queue; once it is healthy there (nginx and SSL set up), the project switches to the target and its containers on the current server are stopped, not removed. When the deploy fails the project keeps running where it is. Persistent volumes are copied once the image is built on the target: the app is stopped on the current server, each volume is streamed over SSH and checked (files, bytes, checksum), then the container starts on the target. On any failure the stopped containers are started again; the volumes on the current server are never removed. Compose stacks, static sites and a linked database on the current server cannot be moved yet.

202.description: The move started; follow the deployment

409.description: A check blocks the move; the message lists why

Known vulnerabilities of the image this deployment started, from the scan run in the background after the deploy succeeded (Trivy on the deploy server). `format=csv` or `format=json` downloads the list as a file. Needs `deployments:read` on an API key. 404 `NO_VULNERABILITY_SCAN` until a scan was recorded; compose stacks, static sites and previews are not scanned.

Audit log of the current organization (admin/owner only). Filter by project, user, action, source (ui, api, webhook, system) and date range (`from`/`to`, inclusive ISO 8601). Paginated with `limit`/`offset`. Secret values are never returned; changed secrets appear as `{ changed: true }`.

put.description: Owner/admin only, off by default. Daily or weekly, the pending OS security updates are applied as by POST /servers/{serverId}/patches/apply (Docker/containerd excluded, never reboots), starting inside a 60-minute maintenance window in UTC. While a deploy is going on on the server the run waits; if that lasts the whole window it is skipped. Every run goes to the audit log and the server timeline.
